# Before the session {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

::: {style="margin-top: 1.0em; color:#F7F4ED"}
### Who writes the rules a multinational actually follows?
:::

## What to do, and how long it takes

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Read Prakash & Potoski (2006); skim Abbott & Snidal and Mattli & Büthe | 75–90 min |
| **2** | Collect ISO Survey, IMF exports, WDI GDP | 45 min + account wait |
| **3** | Attempt the self-check | 15 min |

::: {.warn}
**Start the ISO Survey download two days ahead.** It requires a free IAF CertSearch account.
:::

## 1 · Read

**Prakash & Potoski (2006), *Racing to the Bottom? Trade, Environmental Governance, and ISO 14001*, AJPS 50(2): 350–364**

::: {.muted}
[doi:10.1111/j.1540-5907.2006.00188.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-5907.2006.00188.x)
:::

| | |
|---|---|
| **1** | The **question**: race to the bottom? |
| **2** | The **mechanism**: why do export markets matter? |
| **3** | The **evidence**: which panel, which key variable? |
| **4** | One **limitation** |

::: {.get}
**Skim:** Abbott & Snidal (2009) — *draw the triangle* · Mattli & Büthe (2003) — *write down the three explanations*
:::

## 2 · Collect

| | Dataset | What |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **ISO Survey** | ISO 14001 and ISO 9001 certificates, country × year |
| **2** | **IMF IMTS** | goods exports, your ~35 countries → all partners |
| **3** | **WDI** | GDP, current US$ |

::: {.step}
Cannot download the ISO tables? **Fallback:** transcribe 35 countries × 6 years (2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2024). Details in `data/README.md`.
:::

## 3 · Self-check

1. The three corners of the triangle — place **one** scheme inside it
2. **Race to the bottom** vs **California effect** — which does the paper support?
3. Why would a Vietnamese firm certify to ISO 14001 if no law requires it?
4. Who sits at the table when an ISO standard is written — and why does it matter?

## Arrive with

::: {.check}
- The paper read; the triangle drawn; three explanations written down
- ISO, IMTS and WDI files in `data/raw/`, logged
- Your self-check, on paper
:::
